content: Your medications may interact with other drugs, potentially altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can influence the elimination of clarithromycin from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. Conversely, clarithromycin can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially altering their effects. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For less urgent cases, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, laboratory and medical tests (e.g., cultures, liver and kidney function tests) may be required to monitor your progress and detect potential side effects. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually every 12 hours. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may result in a recurrence of the infection. If you are taking this medication to prevent certain bacterial infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not discontinue the medication without your doctor’s approval. Common side effects may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, and changes in taste. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking clarithromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin, azithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Clarithromycin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (e.g., diuretics or water pills) or if you have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Clarithromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Clarithromycin passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of clarithromycin from your body, which may impact how clarithromycin works. Clarithromycin can also slow the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect how they work.
